title: Changing run endpoints
statement: Let $P$ be a counter program with $R$ natural-number registers and labels in $\Lambda$, run on a binary input $x$. Suppose that for every output word $o$, some run of at most $b$ steps from label $\ell$, register assignment $\rho$, input position $p$, and output $o$ reaches label-or-halt state $\ell'$, assignment $\rho'$, position $p'$, and output $o$ followed by $e$. If $\rho=\sigma$, $\rho'=\sigma'$, $p=q$, $p'=q'$, $e=e'$, and $b\le b'$, then for every $o$ some run of at most $b'$ steps from $\ell,\sigma,q,o$ reaches $\ell',\sigma',q'$ with output $o$ followed by $e'$.
hypotheses_covered: A counter program $P$ with $R$ natural-number registers and label set $\Lambda$
A run relation from $\ell,\rho,p$ to $\ell',\rho',p'$ appending $e$ within bound $b$
replaced:
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$.  Suppose that from label
$\ell$ with registers $\rho$ and $p$ input symbols read, $P$ reaches $\ell'$ (a
label or the halted state) with registers $\rho'$ and $p'$ symbols read within
$b$ steps while appending $e$ to its output, and that $\rho = \sigma$,
$\rho' = \sigma'$, $p = q$, $p' = q'$, $e = e'$ and $b \le b'$.  Then from label
$\ell$ with registers $\sigma$ and $q$ symbols read, $P$ reaches $\ell'$ with
registers $\sigma'$ and $q'$ symbols read within $b'$ steps while appending
$e'$.
